headline: Reviewed $5 million Willow Street grant, $1 million Five Mile Pond beach grant, and $5 million school budget adjustment; no votes taken.
summary: Reviewed donations and grants for parks, the Colonial and Shean Blocks, Five Mile Pond, and housing. Also reviewed a $5 million grant for sidewalks and green space near the Willow Street parking garage, and a grant for water and sewer repairs at Boston Mobile Home Park. Discussed an approximately $5 million FY2027 Springfield Public Schools budget adjustment from increased charter school tuition aid; no formal recommendations or votes were recorded.

SPS Supplemental Budget – Increase in Charter School Tuition State Aid 
 
On October 19, 2026, the Finance Committee, chaired by Councilor Zaida Govan, met to review 
donations, grant awards, and a supplemental adjustment to the school budget. The committee 
acknowledged a donation from the Jeffrey Speller Foundation and reviewed a $425,000 Parkland 
Acquisitions and Renovations for Communities (PARC) grant, matched with a $265,000 
Community Development Block Grant, to improve Hubbard Park's splash pad, playground, and 
accessibility. Additional grants included $450,000 for stabilization of the Colonial Block and 
funding for improvements to the Shean Block at State and Main Streets. 
 
The committee reviewed a $1 million Land and Water Conservation Fund grant, supported by a 
previously approved $1 million City match from free cash, to renovate the public beach area at
Five Mile Pond, including accessible restrooms, parking, playground improvements, and other 
amenities. Construction is anticipated to begin in 2027, with reopening projected for summer 
2028. A grant exceeding $1.2 million, with a $100,000 Community Development Block Grant 
match, will address water and sewer infrastructure deficiencies affecting approximately 312 
households at the Boston Mobile Home Park. The City will oversee contracting and reimburse 
expenses following inspection of completed work. 
 
The committee also reviewed a $5 million grant for sidewalks, street improvements, and public 
green space near the new Willow Street parking garage in the Main Street Convention Center 
District. Council President Tracye Whitfield requested information on grant investments in 
neighborhoods outside downtown, and Planning and Economic Development agreed to provide a 
list of projects and improvements. Discussion concluded with an approximately $5 million 
supplemental FY2027 Springfield Public Schools budget adjustment resulting from increased 
state charter school tuition reimbursement aid. Additional clarification from School Department 
representatives was expected at the City Council meeting. No formal committee 
recommendations or votes were recorded. The meeting adjourned at 5:40 p.m.
